tips.title: Generation and editing tips
items: Describe what each person is doing, where they are looking and how their hands meet the scene.
For an edit, list the face, outfit and framing to preserve before naming one change. Inspect each new image before continuing.
Put exact campaign wording in quotation marks and specify the physical surface carrying it. Check every letter in the result.
For a future video opening, leave room around the people and separate the foreground, subject and background.
Choose PNG and a transparent background when you need an asset with an alpha channel.

prompts.title: Metro exit — MAKE YOUR MOVE
prompts.prompt: A compelling live-action feature-film still, 16:9 widescreen. A fictional woman in her late twenties in a deep burgundy trench coat has just emerged from a Parisian metro stairway into a rain-soaked street at blue hour. She is caught mid-stride, turning toward someone just outside the frame, alert and full of intent; her face is clearly visible, her coat moves in the wind. Several adults cross the street behind her; a passing taxi adds a soft streak of warm light. A large physically printed illuminated advertising panel, nearly front-facing on the right side of the street, reads exactly "MAKE YOUR MOVE" in three beautifully spaced lines of bold off-white sans-serif capitals. These are the only prominent words. The panel belongs naturally to the real location. Reflections on wet pavement, cinematic cyan and amber practical lighting, natural skin texture, believable hands, coherent perspective, rich deep blacks with detail. Shot on a 40mm anamorphic lens, restrained film grain, subtle halation, sophisticated campaign-film composition. The woman and the sign remain comfortably inside the central 80 percent of the image. A real human story in progress, evocative and dynamic, not a posed stock photograph. A single cohesive photograph with no borders or added graphic overlay.

prompts.title: The last train — a moment between two people
prompts.prompt: A cinematic live-action film still, 16:9 widescreen, from a beautifully photographed contemporary drama. On an almost empty covered railway platform at night, a fictional woman around thirty wearing a forest-green jacket reaches back to take the hand of a fictional man around thirty-five in a dark wool coat. They are both walking toward a waiting train; she turns toward him with a small spontaneous smile, while he looks at her with concern and affection. Their faces and connected hands are readable and anatomically natural. Warm light spills from the open train door behind them into the cool blue rain beyond the platform roof. A station worker and two adult travellers remain small in the background, adding scale and a believable lived-in setting. The image catches a real transition, coat hems moving and one foot just leaving the ground. Strong foreground, middle ground and background separation, glistening pavement, delicate steam in the distance, fine natural skin texture and wool detail. 50mm cinema lens, softly rolled highlights, subtle film grain, realistic color separation, intimate and emotionally charged without melodrama. Carefully composed with both people fully legible and room around them for a later camera move. One cohesive physical location, a film frame rather than a fashion pose, no title or graphic overlay.

faqs.q: What is Seedream 5.5, and what can I create?
faqs.a: Seedream 5.5 is an AI image generation and editing model developed by ByteDance. On MaxVideoAI, use text or up to 10 reference images to create portraits, cinematic scenes, campaign images and transparent PNG assets. Each request returns one still image.

faqs.q: How is Seedream 5.5 different from Seedream 5.0 Pro?
faqs.a: ByteDance presents 5.5 as an advance in successive edits, realism and text rendering, with native transparent PNG output. In MaxVideoAI, 5.5 also offers 1K, 1.5K and 2K instead of Pro’s 2K-only output. Both accept up to 10 references and return one image per request. The examples above show selected results, not a controlled head-to-head benchmark.

faqs.q: How do I refine the same scene?
faqs.a: Use the selected image as a reference. State what to preserve and ask for a focused change, then inspect the new result before using it for the next edit.

faqs.q: Can I create a transparent background?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose PNG output and the transparent-background setting. JPEG is suitable for an opaque scene.

faqs.q: Which resolutions and formats are available?
faqs.a: MaxVideoAI offers 1K, 1.5K and 2K, with JPEG or PNG output. Image editing accepts up to 10 references and returns one image; use Lite when you need image sets.

faqs.q: Can I animate the image afterwards?
faqs.a: Save the still and choose a video model for a separate generation. A readable silhouette, clear hands and space around the subject make the opening frame easier to plan.

faqs.q: How much does Seedream 5.5 cost on MaxVideoAI?
faqs.a: MaxVideoAI uses pay-as-you-go credits, with no required subscription. Choose your resolution and references in Create, then review the current price before generating. Each new generation or edit has its own quote.

features.title: Start with a human moment
features.body: A small gesture, a readable expression and a specific location give a portrait or cinematic scene direction. Describe skin, hair and clothing as physical materials.

features.title: Refine with a clear brief
features.body: Use up to 10 references for the people, wardrobe, scene or style. Name what must stay and change one part at a time; review the new result before the next edit.

features.title: Put the message in the scene
features.body: Specify the exact words, line breaks and surface: a station sign, printed poster or painted wall. Keep the copy short enough to inspect.

features.title: Make room for the next use
features.body: Create one JPEG or PNG in 1K, 1.5K or 2K. Use transparent PNG for an isolated asset, or save an opaque scene as a starting still for a separate video model.

referenceWorkflows.title: Guide each reference

referenceWorkflows.title: Continue from the last edit

referenceWorkflows.title: Choose a transparent output
referenceWorkflows.body: Select PNG and Transparent in Create. Describe the isolated subject and leave space around its edges. JPEG cannot preserve transparency.

cinematic.provenance: Generated and reviewed on 13–14 November 2026 with Seedream 5.5 via BytePlus. All people and scenes are AI-generated. The edit sequence uses the previous image as its single reference.

panels.title: Same scene. A new direction.
panels.body: An emerald jacket becomes ivory. Then the warm theatre light becomes cool blue. Compare each edit with its actual source, using the slider or your keyboard.
panels.note: Each request uses one reference: original → wardrobe edit → lighting edit. Inspect the face, hands, curtains and framing; details can still change.

panels.title: Put your words in the world.
panels.body: A theatre entrance, a passing character and a short message inside the scene. Give the text a surface, a position and a reason to be there.
panels.note: The prompt requests “ONE NIGHT ONLY”. This selected image shows the result; check every letter before publishing.

panels.title: Look closer. Stay human.
panels.body: A runner catches her breath. Examine the skin, flyaway hair and textured fabric in this close portrait, then open the original at full size.
panels.note: This selected result illustrates one portrait brief. Inspect facial details and anatomy before using any generated image.

panels.title: Free to move. Ready to compose.
panels.body: Generate an isolated subject with a real alpha channel. Change the preview background to inspect the edges, then open the unchanged original PNG.
panels.note: The dancer is the same image on every background. Transparency was verified in this original and its WebP display copy; no background-removal effect is applied here.

panels.title: How to prompt Seedream 5.5
panels.body: Begin with a moment a camera could capture. Describe the people and their interaction, then the framing, physical light, textures and any exact text.
panels.note: Two independent text-to-image results, with their exact English prompts. Use either as a starting brief for your own scene.

panels.title: Give the moment a story.
panels.body: Build a frame around a choice: a woman stepping into a rainy street, or two people catching the last train. Give the location, gesture and light a job in the story.
panels.note: Two independent text-to-image results, with their exact English prompts. Use either as a starting brief for your own scene.
